tasks.short: Prepare and distribute health education materials

steps.what: Select health evidence and author audience-appropriate education messages
Prepare reports, bulletins and visual aids in recurring formats
Check and distribute the health education materials

tasks.design: Configure recurring publication layouts in {DOCS} from specialist-authored health content. The specialist checks facts, readability and audience fit before distribution through {EMAIL} or the existing physical channel.
tasks.previous_blocker: Content is repeatedly reformatted into recurring bulletins and aids.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates can reuse approved copy without generating health claims.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing correct guidance and making it understandable without misleading simplification.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist understands audience concerns and assesses the message's health meaning.
tasks.altitude: Less layout work with unchanged health-content and release responsibility.

reach.task: Adapt distribution to community access needs

evidence.claim: Native templates can format supplied health content while leaving evidence selection and meaning checks human. This is an E1 design scenario, not a measured education case.

assumptions: Boundary includes authoring, layout and distribution of recurring materials; no clinical advice or source research is automated.

Specialist produces topic, audience, approved wording, source/version, selected visual, dates and distribution instructions in s1. Its unchanged 40 hours include source verification and field capture; missing guidance is resolved manually.
s2 performs layout only; overflow and unusual formats return to s3 for manual correction. Physical printing and handout effort remain in s3.
Test native templates first. Five focal upkeep hours cover format tests and guidance-version checks per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Do templates save layout time after content capture, accessibility review and distribution?

incremental.description: Maintain templates and check guidance versions

approvals.approved_version: Exact final material, source versions, audience and distribution selection; edits require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+0+25=65; gross 35 minus 5 upkeep gives net 30. Low 8 allows 22 hours for unusual layouts and accessibility corrections. Health judgement and distribution retain time; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Develop and maintain cooperative relationships with public health agencies and organizations

tasks.design: Retain relationship development and negotiation with the specialist. Existing partner information in {CRM} can support continuity without replacing trust-building contact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cooperation depends on trust and differing agency priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared contact records support continuity, not demonstrated shorter relationship work.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving competing interests and sustaining commitments.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist earns trust and recognises concerns that are not stated directly.
tasks.altitude: Relationship time and external commitments remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Public-health partnerships require human trust and negotiation; contact databases do not replace that work.

assumptions: Boundary is partnership interaction; contact maintenance is counted in the separate database task.
Partners supply their priorities through the full-time interaction; no machine action or free structured cooperation score is introduced.
Use existing contact access before building tools.
Zero incremental upkeep because the relationship process is unchanged; partner time earns no saving.
research_questions: Which delays arise from contact-data problems rather than necessary relationship work?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0. Relationship work retains its time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain programme information and contact lists

steps.what: Verify programme contact changes and capture permitted uses
Update databases, mailing lists and telephone networks with checked changes
Resolve contact exceptions and accept the programme information updates

tasks.design: Use {CRM} as the maintained contact source and configure staged updates to {EMAIL} lists and {TELEPHONY} directories. The specialist verifies source changes and permitted uses, resolves identity conflicts and accepts the final updates.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same contact change is entered into several lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Native connectors and stable identifiers can reuse checked changes.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous identities, outdated roles and inappropriate sharing of sensitive information.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist knows which programme relationships and uses are appropriate.
tasks.altitude: Less list copying, with contact verification and access decisions retained.

evidence.claim: Stable contact identifiers and native list synchronisation can remove repeated entry; this is an E1 workflow estimate rather than a cited social-care product capability.

assumptions: Boundary is programme directory maintenance, excluding relationship building and activity statistics.

Specialist produces contact identifier, organisation, name, role, verified email/phone, list membership, permitted purpose and source/date in s1. Its full 45 hours include reading messages, clarification and manual entry; unstructured messages are not presumed clean.
s2 stages exact keyed updates only. Conflicting identifiers or unknown permissions remain unchanged until s3 resolves them manually.
Test native contact connectors first. Five focal hours cover mapping failures and access reviews; two other-role support hours maintain connections per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Can checked changes update multiple lists without added identity or permission correction time?

approvals.approved_version: Exact keyed contact changes, list memberships and permitted purposes in the staged batch; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+0+20=65; gross 35 minus 5 upkeep gives net 30. Low 8 allows 22 hours for conflicting or unsupported list updates. Verification remains full time; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Document activities and capture applications, presentations and persons assisted
Compile recorded activity counts into the programme information return
Reconcile activity totals and save the accepted return

tasks.design: Configure activity forms and totals in {OTHER}, the programme records system. Replace separate {SPREADSHEET} tallies with counts from checked records, retaining source capture and reconciliation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activity records are manually recounted for reporting.
tasks.enabler_now: Native grouped counts can apply explicit event and person definitions.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing unique people from attendances and defining completed applications.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist resolves ambiguous activity evidence and explains coverage limits.
tasks.altitude: Less recounting, with reporting definitions and acceptance still human.

evidence.claim: Programme activity totals can be calculated deterministically from keyed records and explicit counting definitions; this is an E1 design estimate.

assumptions: Boundary covers activity capture and return preparation, excluding programme delivery and contact-directory maintenance.

Specialist produces activity identifier, programme identifier, date, type, completion status, attendance count and a permitted pseudonymous person key only when unique-person reporting requires it in s1. Its full 50 hours include capture and source reconciliation; no free attendance feed is assumed.
Programme manager provides counting definitions; added definition review costs two other-role hours. Missing person keys prevent unique-person claims and require manual reconciliation in s3.
Test native forms and grouped reports first. Four focal upkeep hours cover definition tests and exception monitoring per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Do keyed records remove recounting after capture and unique-person reconciliation are included?

incremental.description: Test counting rules and review anomalies

approvals.approved_version: Exact source-record snapshot, counting-definition version, reporting period and totals; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=50+0+20=70; gross 30 minus 4 upkeep gives net 26. Low 8 allows 18 hours for incomplete attendance records. Original activity capture and final reconciliation retain time; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce recurring formatting, list copying and recounting while protecting content judgement and partnerships.
reach: Coordinate data definitions and distribution access with community health workers
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with reliable programme records and more attention available for community needs.
